title: POC data in-transit minimization and DPA clause draft
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working draft for customer POCs focused on minimizing the exposure of customer data while running inference in hosted and hybrid POC topologies. It captures operational patterns, recommended engineering mitigations, and suggested DPA/DPA-addendum contract language we can propose during commercial talks.

Audience:
- Solutions engineering (primary)
- Legal (for clause review)
- Customer security teams (as a discussion artifact)
- Customer success / sales for alignment on ask thresholds

Problem statement (short):
POCs often send customer data to Redwood-hosted endpoints or intermediate proxies for model inference. Customers and their security teams commonly push back on: persistent logs, unredacted storage, telemetry payloads containing PHI/PII, and unclear retention removal timelines. We need a minimal set of patterns + contract text we can offer that balances speed of POC with acceptable legal risk.

Key goals:
- Minimize the amount of customer-identifiable data that traverses Redwood control plane or persists on Redwood-managed storage during POC runs.
- Provide clear, auditable retention windows and deletion guarantees for both request/response payloads and inferred artifacts (embeddings, generated text, metadata).
